angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 194,031 km at 12.48 pc = 0.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 80.1134 +/- 0.0206 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 12.48 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2789 +/- 0.0014 solar radii from Lustig-Yaeger et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LHS 475 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7.1317L/abstract): 194,031 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.262 solar masses from Lustig-Yaeger et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LHS 475 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7.1317L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3300 +/- 80 K from Lustig-Yaeger et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 475 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7.1317L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lustig-Yaeger et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 475 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023NatAs...7.1317L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lhs-475.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.965, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
